Home.aboutTitle: A free football simulator for the top leagues
Home.aboutBody: Foot Simu is a free football simulator for the Premier League, Championship, League One, League Two, La Liga, Segunda División, Bundesliga, 2. Bundesliga, Serie A, Serie B, Ligue 1, Ligue 2, Primeira Liga, Eredivisie, Eerste Divisie, Brasileirão Série A and Série B, the Argentine, Chilean, Colombian, Uruguayan, Paraguayan, Ecuadorian and Peruvian top divisions, Liga MX, MLS, the FA Cup, the Copa do Brasil, the Copa del Rey, the Coppa Italia, the DFB-Pokal, the Champions League, the Europa League, the Conference League, the Copa Libertadores and the Copa Sudamericana. Each league starts from the real table and fixtures. Type your own predictions or simulate the remaining matches, and see how the title race, the European places and the relegation battle could end.

annualNotes.ARG: The Copa Argentina winner also qualifies, and the last club in the three-season averages table is also relegated (not shown).
annualNotes.COL: The Copa BetPlay winner also goes to the Copa Sudamericana. Relegation is decided by the averages table (not shown).
annualNotes.URU: Approximate: the Uruguayan champion and runner-up, decided by the tournament winners' play-off, also go to the Copa Libertadores, and the official rules may differ. Relegation is decided by the averages table (not shown).
annualNotes.PAR: The places follow the usual allocation; the official rules for this season may differ. Relegation is decided by the averages table (not shown).
annualNotes.PER: Approximate: the Copa Libertadores places are decided by a play-off between the tournament champions and the best-placed clubs, and the official rules may differ. Points deductions are those in ESPN's current standings.

Seo.intro: Use the {simulator} to predict the rest of the {league} {season} season ({aka}). Type your own scores or simulate the remaining matches: the table updates instantly with the official tiebreakers and the qualification and relegation zones.
Seo.introPlayoffs: Use the {simulator} to predict the rest of the {league} {season} season ({aka}). Type your own scores or simulate the remaining matches: the Eastern and Western Conference tables update instantly with the official tiebreakers and the playoff and wild-card places.
Seo.step1: Choose a matchday and type a score for each match, or use the dice to simulate it.
Seo.step2: Press Simulate matchday or Simulate rest of season to play the remaining fixtures in one click.
Seo.step3: Open the Chances tab to see every team's chances of the title, Europe and relegation.
Seo.step3Playoffs: Open the Chances tab to see every team's chances of finishing first in its conference and of reaching the playoffs.
Seo.introCup: Use the {simulator} to predict the rest of the {league} {season} ({aka}). Type your own scores or simulate each round: a tie that ends level goes to penalties, the winners go into the hat, and the rounds not yet drawn get a simulated draw that the real one replaces when it is made.

Seo.step2Cup: Press Simulate round or Simulate to the final. The next round is drawn from the winners; New draw reshuffles a simulated draw.
Seo.step3Cup: Open the Chances tab to see every club's chance of reaching each round and of winning the cup.
Seo.introCupBracket: Use the {simulator} to predict the rest of the {league} {season} ({aka}). Type your own scores or simulate each round: a tie that ends level goes to penalties, and the winners move on along the fixed bracket, with no draws.
Seo.step2CupBracket: Press Simulate round or Simulate to the final. The winners move on along the fixed bracket.
Seo.introContinental: Use the {simulator} to predict the rest of the {league} {season} ({aka}). Type your own scores or simulate the league phase: the 36-club table updates instantly with UEFA's tiebreakers. The top 8 go straight to the round of 16, 9th to 24th play the knockout play-off, and the knockout phase can be played all the way to the final.
Seo.step3Continental: Open the Chances tab to see every club's chance of finishing in the top 8, of reaching the knockout phase, of reaching the final and of winning the {league}.

introContinentalGroups.LIB: Use the {simulator} to predict the rest of the {league} {season} ({aka}). Type your own scores or simulate the group stage: the eight group tables update instantly. The top two of each group go to the round of 16 and third place drops into the Copa Sudamericana, then the knockout phase can be played all the way to the final.
introContinentalGroups.SUD: Use the {simulator} to predict the rest of the {league} {season} ({aka}). Type your own scores or simulate the group stage: the eight group tables update instantly. Group winners go straight to the round of 16, runners-up play a knockout play-off against the clubs dropping in from the Copa Libertadores, and the knockout phase can be played all the way to the final.

step3ContinentalGroups.LIB: Open the Chances tab to see every club's chance of finishing in its group's top two, of reaching the final and of winning the {league}.
step3ContinentalGroups.SUD: Open the Chances tab to see every club's chance of winning its group, of finishing in its group's top two, of reaching the final and of winning the {league}.

Seo.introZones: Use the {simulator} to predict the rest of the {league} {season} ({aka}). Type your own scores or simulate the remaining matches: both zone tables update instantly with the official tiebreakers. The top 8 of each zone go to the play-offs, played across the zones (1st in Zone A v 8th in Zone B…) in single matches down to the final. league.q: How are the title and relegation chances calculated?
league.a: The Chances tab plays out the rest of the season 10,000 times from the current table, including your own predictions, and counts how often each team finishes in each position.
Yes. Your predictions are saved in your browser, so they are still there when you come back. Use Share to send a link that shows exactly your table.

home.a: Foot Simu is a free football simulator. Pick a league, predict or simulate the remaining matches and watch the table change live.

The Premier League, Championship, League One, League Two, La Liga, Segunda División, Bundesliga, 2. Bundesliga, Serie A, Serie B, Ligue 1, Ligue 2, Primeira Liga, Eredivisie, Eerste Divisie, Brasileirão Série A and Série B, the Argentine, Chilean, Colombian, Uruguayan, Paraguayan, Ecuadorian and Peruvian top divisions, Liga MX, MLS, the FA Cup, the Copa do Brasil, the Copa del Rey, the Coppa Italia, the DFB-Pokal, the Champions League, the Europa League, the Conference League, the Copa Libertadores and the Copa Sudamericana, with real fixtures and results for the current season.

home.q: How does the football simulator decide results?
home.a: Each simulated score is drawn from the attack and defence each team has shown this season, with home advantage. Strong teams win more often, but upsets still happen.
No. Foot Simu is free, your predictions are saved in your browser and you can share them with a link.

cup.a: It starts from the real {league} {season} draw and results. {ratingNote} A tie that ends level is decided on penalties.

Once a round is decided, the next round is drawn at random from the winners (plus the clubs entering). The simulated draw stays the same when you reload or share the page; New draw reshuffles it, and the real draw replaces it as soon as it is made.
The Chances tab plays the rest of the cup 5,000 times from the current results, drawing the undrawn rounds afresh each time, and counts how often each club reaches each round and wins the cup.
Yes. Your predictions are saved in your browser, so they are still there when you come back. Use Share to send a link that shows exactly your bracket.

cupBracket.a: It starts from the real {league} {season} bracket and results. {ratingNote} A tie that ends level is decided on penalties.

No. The {league} is played on a fixed bracket set before the season, so every pairing from the round of 16 to the final is known in advance: each round's winners meet the winners of the neighbouring tie.
The Chances tab plays the rest of the cup 5,000 times from the current results along the fixed bracket, and counts how often each club reaches each round and wins the cup.
Yes. Your predictions are saved in your browser, so they are still there when you come back. Use Share to send a link that shows exactly your bracket.

continental.a: It starts from the real {league} {season} league-phase table and fixtures. Type a score for any remaining match or press Simulate: the table updates instantly with UEFA's tiebreakers. Once the league phase is complete, the knockout phase is seeded from the table and can be played to the final.

Clubs come from many leagues, so each club starts from its form in its own league this season, scaled by how strong that league is (clubs from leagues not on Foot Simu start from a default for the competition). Their results in the {league} then update the rating as the season goes on.

continental.q: How is the knockout phase decided?
continental.a: The top 8 go straight to the round of 16. The clubs finishing 9th to 24th play a two-legged knockout play-off, 9th–16th against 17th–24th, and the winners meet the top 8 in the round of 16. The better-placed club in the league phase plays the second leg at home, and a tie level on aggregate goes to extra time and penalties. The final is a single match. Until the real draw, the pairings follow the seeding.

The Chances tab plays the rest of the league phase and the whole knockout phase 5,000 times from the current results, including your predictions on the league phase, and counts how often each club finishes in the top 8 and the top 24, reaches the final and wins the {league}.
Yes. Foot Simu is completely free and you don't need an account.

LIB.a: It starts from the real {league} {season} group tables and fixtures (the qualifying stages before the groups aren't included). Type a score for any remaining match or press Simulate: the group tables update instantly. Once the group stage is complete, the knockout phase is seeded from the tables and can be played to the final.

Clubs come from many countries, so Brazilian clubs start from their form in the Brasileirão this season, scaled by the division, and clubs from leagues not on Foot Simu start from a default for the competition. Their results in the {league} then update the rating as the season goes on.

LIB.q: How is the knockout phase decided?
LIB.a: The group winners, ranked 1st to 8th by their group record, meet the runners-up, ranked 9th to 16th, in a two-legged round of 16. The better-ranked club plays the second leg at home in every round, and a tie level on aggregate goes straight to penalties. The final is a single match. Until the real draw, the pairings follow the seeding.

The Chances tab plays the rest of the group stage and the whole knockout phase 5,000 times from the current results, including your predictions on the group stage, and counts how often each club finishes in its group's top two, reaches the final and wins the {league}.
Yes. Foot Simu is completely free and you don't need an account.

SUD.a: It starts from the real {league} {season} group tables and fixtures (the qualifying stages before the groups aren't included). Type a score for any remaining match or press Simulate: the group tables update instantly. Once the group stage is complete, the knockout phase is seeded from the tables and can be played to the final.

Clubs come from many countries, so Brazilian clubs start from their form in the Brasileirão this season, scaled by the division, and clubs from leagues not on Foot Simu start from a default for the competition. Their results in the {league} then update the rating as the season goes on.

SUD.q: How is the knockout phase decided?
SUD.a: Group winners, ranked 1st to 8th by their group record, go straight to the round of 16. Runners-up, ranked 9th to 16th, play a two-legged knockout play-off against the eight clubs that finished 3rd in the Copa Libertadores groups (17th to 24th), and the winners meet the group winners in the round of 16. The better-ranked club plays the second leg at home in every round, and a tie level on aggregate goes straight to penalties. The final is a single match. Until the real draw, the pairings follow the seeding.

The Chances tab plays the rest of the group stage and the whole knockout phase 5,000 times from the current results, including your predictions on the group stage, and counts how often each club wins its group, finishes in its group's top two, reaches the final and wins the {league}.
Yes. Foot Simu is completely free and you don't need an account.

zones.a: It starts from the real {league} {season} zone tables and fixtures. Type a score for any remaining match or press Simulate: each result is drawn from the attack and defence each team has shown this season, with home advantage, and the tables update instantly. Once the zones are complete, the play-offs can be played to the final.

The top 8 of each zone qualify. The round of 16 crosses the zones: 1st in Zone A v 8th in Zone B, 1st in Zone B v 8th in Zone A, 2nd v 7th and so on, at the better-placed club's ground. The bracket is fixed from there. A level match goes straight to penalties, and the final is played at a neutral ground.

zones.q: What about the Copa Libertadores places and relegation?
zones.a: They come from the annual table, which adds up both tournaments' regular phases for all 30 clubs: open it with the switch above the table. The Apertura and Clausura champions and the Copa Argentina winner go to the Copa Libertadores with the top 3 not already in, the next 6 to the Copa Sudamericana, and the last club is relegated. A second club goes down from the three-season averages table, which isn't modelled here.

The Chances tab plays out the rest of the tournament and the play-offs 5,000 times from the current results, including your predictions, and counts how often each club finishes first in its zone, reaches the play-offs and wins the title.
Yes. Foot Simu is completely free and you don't need an account.

tournaments.a: It starts from the real {league} {season} tables and fixtures of every tournament of the year. Type a score for any remaining match or press Simulate: each result is drawn from the attack and defence each team has shown this season, with home advantage, and the tables update instantly.

The {league} plays more than one tournament a year, each with its own champion. Use the switch above the table to move between them. The annual table adds up all of them and decides the places in the Copa Libertadores and the Copa Sudamericana.
It is decided by the averages table (points per game over the last seasons), which isn't modelled here.

The Chances tab plays out the rest of the tournament (and its play-offs, where it has them) 10,000 times from the current results, including your predictions, and counts how often each club finishes in each position.
Yes. Foot Simu is completely free and you don't need an account.

liguilla.a: It starts from the real {league} {season} table and fixtures. Type a score for any remaining match or press Simulate: each result is drawn from the attack and defence each team has shown this season, with home advantage, and the table updates instantly. Once the regular phase is over, the Liguilla can be played to the final.

The top 8 qualify. The quarter-finals are 1st v 8th, 2nd v 7th, 3rd v 6th and 4th v 5th, and the semi-finals are re-seeded: the best-placed club left plays the lowest. Every round is played over two legs with the better-placed club at home in the second. A tie level on aggregate goes to the better-placed club, except in the final, which goes to extra time and penalties.

The Chances tab plays out the rest of the tournament and the Liguilla 5,000 times from the current results, including your predictions, and counts how often each club finishes in each position and wins the title.
Yes. Your predictions are saved in your browser, so they are still there when you come back. Use Share to send a link that shows exactly your table.
Yes. Foot Simu is completely free and you don't need an account.

ratingNote.FAC: Each club's strength comes from its own league this season (Premier League, Championship, League One or League Two), scaled by the division; non-league clubs are rated below League Two.
ratingNote.CDB: Each club's strength comes from its own league this season (Série A or Série B), scaled by the division; clubs from Série C, Série D and the state leagues are rated below Série B.
ratingNote.CDR: Each club's strength comes from its own league this season (La Liga or Segunda División), scaled by the division; clubs from Primera Federación and below are rated under Segunda.
ratingNote.CIT: Each club's strength comes from its own league this season (Serie A or Serie B), scaled by the division; Serie C clubs are rated below Serie B. There is no draw: the Coppa Italia follows a fixed bracket.
ratingNote.DFB: Each club's strength comes from its own league this season (Bundesliga or 2. Bundesliga), scaled by the division; 3. Liga and amateur clubs are rated below the 2. Bundesliga. An amateur club drawn against a professional one plays at home.
